title: Skydance Is Merging Paramount And Warner Bros.’ Game Studios Into One Unit
description: With Paramount's $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery in the bag, details on what this merger means for the Warner Bros. game division have finally been revealed. Warner Bros. Interactive will merge with the newly formed Paramount Games Studio, and it'll oversee projects based on Skydance's rich--and newly acquired-library of IP. That lineup includes Avatar: The Last Airbender, South Park, Mortal Kombat, Game of Thrones, and Star Trek--and that's not even mentioning the treasure trove of DC Comics IP that the company now owns. The new division will be overseen by Tony Driscoll, president of games and experiences at Skydance, and one of the executives leading corporate strategy and development at the company. Driscoll had previously described video games as a "core pillar" of entertainment, alongside film and TV. SpongeBob Mortal Kombat crossover when? "We’re investing in our future growth engines alongside our core ambitions in TV, film and direct-to-consumer: Games, experiences, consumer products, and publishing," Gordon wrote in a staff memo (via Variety ). "These are core pillars of our strategy to build engagement and fandom in both the physical and digital worlds. We want to meet consumers where they watch, play, and engage." It's still unclear what the future plans are for the growing Skydance gaming division, or how hard it'll be hit by looming layoffs. This branch of Skydance will now be the home to some big WBI developers like Avalanche Software (Hogwarts Legacy), NetherRealm Studios (Mortal Kombat), Rocksteady Studios (Batman: Arkham Series and one Suicide Squad game I don't want to talk about), and TT Games (Various Lego games). Former Activision CEO Bobby Kotick has also joined the board of directors, and Skydance is also producing the Call of Duty movie with Activision, which is scheduled to hit theaters in 2028.

title: "Your body is foreign territory": Small-town mystery puzzler Patience is a Virtue explores power and vulnerability by way of a unique conversation system
description: The English language can be a way of communicating, and it can be a way of subjugating. Patience is a Virtue protagonist Louis knows this intimately. In this "cozy-meets-creepy" conversation puzzle game from teaisfortoby!, some interactions require you to answer only using the words spoken by the other party. The first such chat in the demo is with Louis's boss at the local grocery store. She wants him to lock up early. All Louis has to do is assent. But to assent, he must reassemble her phrasing into a coherent, five-word response, grappling not just with elementary grammar but phantom questions of tone. Being the first of these puzzles, it's an easier one, but the constraint is rather suffocating nonetheless. Louis is chronically ill and neurodivergent, and his difficulty talking back reflects his lack of privilege. These words don't belong to him. They are alien objects he must painstakingly bolt together on demand. Read more

title: Resident Evil Requiem DLC Could Further Rewrite One Of The Series’ Biggest Villains
description: Resident Evil Requiem is one of this year's biggest hits, and Capcom plans to build on that success with new story DLC. While it hasn't yet revealed when it'll be out or what it's about, one of the game's writers, Haris Orkin, recently teased that the DLC will shed new light on Oswell E. Spencer, one of the biggest villains in the Resident Evil series. "I think villains honestly are really fun to write, because I usually see every villain as a hero of their own story. So the villain is like in their mind they're a hero," Orkin said in an interview with the Distance Nerding podcast. I mean, Victor Gideon thinks he's going to save the world in Requiem. We have an arc for Spencer in Requiem. "Where you understand that more. And then in the DLC you will understand that even further. I probably shouldn't say that, but yeah." Resident Evil Requiem spoilers below Compared to his appearances in previous Resident Evil games, Oswell E. Spencer is more sympathetic, harboring genuine regret for his role in establishing the Umbrella Corporation, his research on the Progenitor Virus, and his ambitious goal of remaking the world with his bioweapons. As revealed in Requiem-- and spoilers if you haven't played it yet --Spencer adopted a baby girl called Grace in 2001, and he successfully developed the powerful antiviral Elpis so that he could eliminate all Progenitor-based viral weapons, as part of his mission to atone for his sins. That version of Spencer is narratively at odds with the version we see in Resident Evil 5, as before his death in 2006 at the hands of Albert Wesker, he was a bit of a bastard who apparently still harbored delusions of grandeur and had started work on a new virus to help him become immortal. Then again, Capcom has been rewriting Resident Evil lore with its remakes, and this new version of Spencer is arguably more fascinating than a stereotypical mustache-twirling villain. While we don't know if Capcom plans to eventually make Resident Evil 5--one of the…

title: GTA 6 PC Release Date Estimate, Rumors, And News
description: Grand Theft Auto 6 is almost here. Well, almost here for console players, anyway. Rockstar's hugely anticipated open-world crime game is officially scheduled to launch on November 19, 2026, for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, but PC players will have to wait a little longer before they can dive in. GTA 6 PC release date estimate Our best guess for the GTA 6 PC release date is Q1 2028, putting the PC version roughly 15-18 months after the console launch. That's not based on a leak or any insider claim; instead we've looked at Rockstar's history of later PC release dates to inform our estimate. That's earlier than the 19-month wait that PC players endured for GTA 5, and later than the 12-month gap between Red Dead Redemption 2's console and PC releases. We're more confident in this estimate since Twitch CEO Dan Clancy let slip that GTA 6 Online would be sometime in 2027. Clancy theorized a bump to Twitch viewership in 2027 "when they launch multiplayer." This could mean Rockstar plans to refine and release the GTA 6 multiplayer experience prior to the PC release. Having said that, Rockstar hasn't officially announced a PC version of GTA 6 at all. The company currently only lists PS6 and Xbox Series X|S as official platforms for the game. However, it would be incredibly surprising if GTA 6 never came to PC. Rockstar's last two major releases eventually made the jump, and Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick has repeatedly acknowledged how important PC has become to the business. Why isn't GTA 6 coming to PC at launch? Zelnick explained earlier in 2026 that Rockstar traditionally prioritizes its core audience on console first. He specifically rejected the idea that a PlayStation marketing agreement was responsible for GTA 6 skipping PC at launch, reiterating that Rockstar has historically gone to console first. Zelnick also said that PC can now account for 45-50% of sales for a major title, compared with a much smaller share when he joined the company. A PC version of GTA 6 therefore…

title: GTA 6 Will Not Stream To PC Through Xbox, Despite Earlier Report
description: PC players hoping to find a way to play GTA 6 when it launches on consoles next month must be feeling pretty disappointed, as Microsoft has clarified that Grand Theft Auto 6 will not be available to stream to PC via Xbox Cloud Gaming. The news follows an earlier report claiming Xbox had secured exclusive streaming rights to Rockstar's highly anticipated game. The clarification came from Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball, who addressed The Verge 's report. Ball said the excitement surrounding GTA 6 and Xbox had resulted in some inaccurate reporting. His full statement read, "While the excitement for GTA 6 and Xbox is great to see, it has also led to some misreporting. We are looking forward to launching GTA 6 on Xbox November 19, though the game will not be streaming exclusively or to PC." That means, sadly for PC players, that you shouldn't expect to fire up Xbox Cloud Gaming on November 19 and find yourself wandering around Vice City without a console. The original report from The Verge claimed that Microsoft had secured exclusive game-streaming rights for GTA 6, citing sources familiar with the company's plans. The report followed comments from Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, who apparently told employees that Microsoft was preparing to do something with GTA 6 that "no other platform holder is doing." The report suggested the arrangement could have been significant for PC players, who as of yet don't know when they'll be able to get their hands on the game. Rockstar has yet to announce a PC version of GTA 6, which is officially confirmed for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. A streaming arrangement could have offered PC players a way to play the game at launch without waiting for the GTA 6 PC release date. The confusion arrives at a pretty interesting time for Xbox Cloud Gaming. Microsoft is making significant changes to the service in November, including introducing a pay-as-you-go option and changing the amount of cloud gaming time available across Game Pass…

title: A Scary-Looking New Conjuring Game Just Got Announced, And It’s Out Next Week On Netflix
description: Out of nowhere, Netflix and Until Dawn developer Supermassive Games announced a new The Conjuring game, and it's out next week. The Conjuring: Unspoken releases on October 13 through Netflix, so you don't need any dedicated hardware or controller to play it. The game is an "interactive paranormal investigation" experience where players decide how the story progresses based on the dialogue options they choose. Players use their phone to walk through the fictional Red Lion Inn to search for clues about "things that go bump in the night," Netflix said. You play as demonologist Francesca Noakes, and you'll use an electromagnetic field reader, an infrared camera, and spirit box to hunt for ghosts. Netflix said you don't need to know anything about The Conjuring to enjoy Unspoken, but people familiar with the series will get "a lot more from the experience." "There are a few familiar faces that pop up in the game, and knowing the backstory adds to the overall impact," Netflix said. Unspoken will be available on Netflix on October 13. It was made in partnership with Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment, whose parent company, Warner Bros. Discovery, was just acquired by Paramount/Skydance.

title: Xbox Was At An “All Time Low,” But Is Now Growing Again CEO Says Without Providing Any Real Evidence
description: During a town hall meeting today, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma spoke to staff to help reassure them following mass layoffs and studio closures related to the "reset" of the business. Windows Central reports that Sharma told staff that Xbox is "making the right decisions" and that "after an all time low, we've started to return to growth," though she did not share any specifics. She added that Gears of War: E-Day, Minecraft Dungeons 2, and World of Warcraft: Forever had "strong" starts, though she did not share any specifics. Sharma said, "We've started to return to growth, more than 2 to 3 times what we were, and we expect that continue." She did not share any specifics about what "2 to 3 times" actually means, though. Sharma also told staff that Xbox's "Gen-10" platform--AKA Project Helix--will be, as rumored, a "family of devices" because "there is no one device that fits all." She said it's important for Xbox to have a "great console first," but there will also be options for players who are "on the go." Sharma went on to say that Microsoft will manufacture some of these devices, and others Microsoft will find partners for. "So, we will be sharing more about that as our plans develop. The operating system is starting to look really good. We're very excited about this," she said. Sharma didn't get into specifics about its next console or portable devices, but they're in the works amidst a very challenging time given the AI-fueled demand for memory and components. The global macroeconomic environment that has driven up oil prices has also rocked markets. Not only this, but in the US, the Federal Reserve recently raised rates, impacting borrowing costs with the effects trickling through various market categories, including gaming. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella praised Sharma for making such deep and extensive cuts at Xbox. title: There’s Never Been A Better Time To Play Fire Emblem: Awakening
description: The world is a complicated place, but, regardless of political leanings, I think we can all agree that in 2016 I was much younger than I am in 2026. The younger me was a much more patient person, especially when it came to playing video games. I relished the opportunity to go on whatever ride designers and developers had spent years meticulously crafting. These days, however, I find myself frantically looking for the shortest and quickest path to satisfaction. Time is a commodity and I am not rich in it. Maybe it's my patience wearing thin, or maybe it's the children who are wrong, but I find that games these days are working overtime to put as much distance between the player and the thing that makes playing it satisfying and worthwhile. Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave is undoubtedly the best recent example of this happening. I love tactics games. I'm not great at them, but nevertheless, I relish the opportunity to slowly move units around squares, compare stats, and then watch them bonk each other. To me, they are the video game equivalent of waking up on a Saturday morning and sitting down to do a sudoku puzzle or fill out a crossword. Like I said, OLD. Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, however, has been the equivalent of being old and waking up on a Saturday morning to find I've got bills to pay, family members to call, meals to prep, mandatory exercise sessions to do, six different gods to appease, and a neighbor that accosts me in the hallway to tell me about their mundanity-riddled week. Each time I turn on Fortune's Weave, I find that the thing I want to do most is buried underneath a laundry list of chores that, while beneficial to my ongoing existence, are also incredibly tedious to the extent that by the time I get to the bit where I can make my little people bonk each with different damage values, I don't even have the mental energy to enjoy making my little people bonk each other. Fortune's Weave has excellent tactical gameplay. It's very engaging and more…

title: You’re Likely Playing Star Wars: Galactic Racer All Wrong, Like I Did For My First 16 Hours
description: I've been loving Star Wars: Galactic Racer --I still cannot believe that a silly racing roguelite is one of my favorite games this year. But as it happens, I could have been enjoying it way more this entire time, because for the first 16 hours or so I've played, I've been playing all wrong: in third-person perspective. I'm still not sure how I didn't know that Galactic Racer allows you to race from the perspective of your pilot, Shade. Like, obviously, it would. It's not an uncommon practice for an arcade racer to have the option to change your perspective from third- to first-person, so why wouldn't Galactic Racer also have that choice? But it wasn't until after I had finished my review and was excitedly talking about the game to a friend and was showing them a trailer that I noticed some of the gameplay being in first-person. "Surely, this must be just cinematic flair or something," I thought. Nope. Anyone who simply opens the settings menu and looks at the controls will see that there's a button to change your perspective. The game never teaches you this; you just need to know to go looking for it in the settings. I immediately jumped into a quick arcade challenge to test it, and, turns out, first-person perspective is 100% the way to play this game. Playing this way doesn't alter Galactic Racer so completely that it feels like a different game, but it makes the already-frenetic speed of skirting around a sharp corner or slipping through a tight squeeze feel even more frantic, and the shaking rumble of every collision with the environment or another racer far more discombobulating. It ups the feeling that you're piloting a death machine being held together with hopes and dreams (and maybe duct tape) to a delightfully tense degree. I love it. In my Galactic Racer review, I talked about how the punishing nature of the roguelite loop creates a palpable pressure to perform well in every race (something that the main story doesn't deliver with its dialogue alone),…

title: Razer’s Wolverine V4 Controller Is Overkill For Most Gamers, And That’s The Point
description: Razer has officially revealed the next entry in its line of high-end gaming controllers, the Wolverine V4 for Xbox and PC. Geared toward competitive gamers--not that there's anything stopping you from using it to play Vampire Survivors--and it focuses primarily on polling performance and thumbstick sensor architecture. One of the biggest changes is Razer choosing capacitive contactless sensors backed by a 16-bit analog-to-digital converter (ADC) for the thumbsticks, rather than the usual Hall Effect magnetic sensor. While Hall Effect thumbsticks are popular for their durability and for essentially eliminating stick drift, they can be prone to magnetic interference. Not a dealbreaker if you're playing at home, but in a competitive scene where victory is measured in fractions of a second, this can be an issue. In comparison, Razer is aiming to offer the same drift resistance, finer granularity, and smoother signal tracking with capacitive sensing. Then there's the polling rate, which is absurdly high. For example, a DualSense Edge is capable of offering up to 1,000Hz (1 ms to 8 ms input latency), but the Wolverine V4 pushes that number up to 8,000Hz in both its wired and wireless configurations when used on PC, which, in theory, should put that on par with high-end esports mice and keyboards. This isn't the first Razer controller to feature an 8,000Hz polling rate, as the Wolverine V3 Pro was also equipped to reach those numbers. Just don't expect to reach those levels on Xbox Series X|S, as hardware limitations cap the refresh rate at 250Hz, meaning the 8,000Hz benefit is strictly for PC competitive gaming. The controller also offers four removable magnetic back buttons and two top claw-grip bumpers, with a modular magnetic design that lets players quickly swap components out, stripping the controller of unused buttons and extra weight. First-person shooter players can also use a back-mounted physical toggle switch with software-tunable actuation points, allowing…

title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer Continues The Hilarious Running Gag That Anakin Is The Boogeyman
description: Anakin Skywalker's purpose in the more recent Star Wars video games has continuously been hilarious to me. For years, Anakin, who eventually became series antagonist Darth Vader, was characterized as something of a superhero who fell to darkness and became a supervillain. He was stronger than the typical guy, but we didn't see many examples of how that strength might be perceived outside of the scope of above-average combat prowess and reflexes. When it was released in 2016, Rogue One was a big departure to that, with its infamous ending scene that gives us a sense of what facing Darth Vader looks like to the average soldier. Turns out, it's terrifying. Anakin is basically an unstoppable demon, and the games since Rogue One have continued to refer back to this notion of him being a living legend. Whether it's adult Anakin fighting like a demigod, Vader rampaging like an unkillable myth, or little Anakin haunting the mind of an elderly superstar racer, I enjoy this continued pattern of almost every Star Wars video game since Rogue One including one small scene, sequence, or conversation that reminds you that the rest of the galaxy thinks Anakin is the straight-up boogeyman. And the superb Star Wars: Galactic Racer, despite being a racing game where you might not expect this to come up, is no exception. Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order is the first major example of this trend. As Jedi-on-the-run Cal, you struggle against the powerful Imperial Inquisitor Second Sister for the entire story, and then when you finally manage to beat her in this tense final lightsaber duel, she's cut down during a surprise appearance by Darth Vader. Vader then goes on to use the Force to break the world around Cal just by walking toward him, as if the very universe bends in his presence. Lightsaber attacks don't work. Cal's Force powers aren't strong enough to affect him. All you can really do is run, and it's a terrifying end to a great game. Star Wars Jedi: Survivor has you face off against…

title: 7 Things I Wish I Knew Before I Played Star Wars: Galactic Racer
description: Soaring spaceships are no stranger to Star Wars video games, with thrilling dogfights at the core of both EA’s Battlefront and Star Wars: Squadrons. Yet very few George Lucas gaming adaptations have swapped aerial showdowns for laps around the intergalactic racetrack--until Galactic Racer. Helmed by talent that worked on the vehicular sections of Battlefront and racing classics like Burnout and Need for Speed, Galactic Racer is a game purely about the thrill of zooming past the Galaxy’s greatest racers, and thanks to its roguelike structure, this tournament plays dirty. As you soar across the dunes of Jaaku and cruise across Lantaana’s lava-filled caverns, it’s important to race prepared. Where some racers may have the backing of insidious forces, we at GameSpot like to support the underdog. So in order to make sure you secure those podium finishes--and give repulsive mining magnate Kestar Bool a run for his money--here are all the Galactic Racer tips you’ll need to finish first in a galaxy far, far away. Cool your jets; learn to master your Afterburner and fear your Ramjet Armed with both a classic boost in the form of an Afterburner and then a souped-up thruster called a Ramjet, it’s all too easy to send your vehicle hurtling into a nearby corner. Yet it’s not just a badly judged turn that can cause your speeder to explode. Making use of the aforementioned turbo-charged Ramjet becomes a sweaty exercise in risk and reward. Push the souped-up boost to its limits and the thruster will quickly start to overheat as you lurch forward. This phase is called redlining, and is about as sweat-inducing as boosting in a game gets. While redlining sends your ship lurching forward, redline too long, however, and your ramjet will detonate in a torrent of flames. As you progress through each tour, you’ll unlock new abilities, parts, and vehicles that can help you extend your redline time and mitigate engine damage. Avoid Eliminator races until you’ve leveled up your speeder In…

title: Call Of Duty’s Richtofen Actor Wants Him To Come Back, Says 2027’s CoD Could Be From Sledgehammer
description: Veteran video game actor Nolan North has addressed his future in the Call of Duty series, saying he hopes to reprise his character Dr. Edward Richtofen from Black Ops' popular Zombies mode. If this does happen, it probably won't be soon. That's because, North said he believes 2027's Call of Duty game might be developed by Sledgehammer. Given that, a new Black Ops game might not come until 2028 at the soonest, but this is just conjecture. Speaking at Gamergy in Puerto Rico ( via DomTheBomb ), North said he hopes Richtofen's story continues in a future Black Ops game, whenever that might be. "I always like when they leave things open for the next one. I know that Infinity Ward and I think Sledgehammer has the next two before there is another Black Ops. I just don't want it to be the end of Richtofen, and I don't think it is," he said. North clarified that he does not know for sure that Richotfen's story will continue, so he hoped people wouldn't think he had some inside knowledge apart from his own hope and belief. Whatever the case, North said Richotofen is one of his favorite characters to voice, and he hopes to reprise him someday. North first appeared as Richtofen in 2008's World at War, and has reprised the role many times over in subsequent games from developer Treyarch. He's a fan-favorite character in the fan-favorite Zombies mode, with the story taking numerous twists and turns over the years. "It's been such a pleasure getting to work with my friends for so long, just like Uncharted was," he said. On the subject of Uncharted, North said he hopes to come back to play Nathan Drake once more. As it happens, rumors are swirling that Naughty Dog is working on Uncharted 5 and that Drake might have a role in it. Regarding North's statement that Sledgehammer is working on the 2027 Call of Duty game, that's not confirmed, but doesn't seem outrageous given this has been reported since 2024. title: Solo Horror Dev Makes A Creepy Connection To A Real Haunted Island In Mexico
description: Being a haunted doll must be difficult. You're missing an eyeball, and your lipstick makes you look more like a cannibal than a cherub. People make faces of disgust at you in the antique mall, and you want to tell them you're actually the unblemished soul of a 19th century nun named Eunice, but they speed away before you can. But if you were a haunted doll, you'd at least have solo developer Steelkrill Studio on your side, as its upcoming survival horror game Where Dolls Hang features real-life creepy dolls looking proudly injured. The dolls of Mexico's Isla de las Muñecas, the Island of the Dolls, have been through a lot over the past 80 years. Folklore suggests the bald dolls cobwebbed and nailed to the island's trees contain the spirit of a drowned little girl, who caretaker Don Julian Santana may or may not have made up. In any case, he spent much of his life fishing plastic Barbies and babies out of the water near his home to honor her spirit. So Where Dolls Hang, which was featured in the Horror Game Awards' recent showcase this past summer, is a tribute, too--it honors the fact that our real world is often freakier than fiction. "Some of the doll models you'll find were created using real photographs," developer Steelkrill explains on Twitter. "The photographs can also be found around in the game." An accompanying clip of first-person gameplay footage demonstrates with an image of a doll head coated completely in dirt and little pimples from raindrops. The Where Dolls Hang player then drops the photo and stares ahead; the same pimply doll head is sticking from a pike right in front of them. "It creates an unusual connection between the game's horrors and reality: something disturbing hanging in a room or sitting in the darkness may not have been designed entirely from imagination," a press release says. "Somewhere in the world, there may be a real photograph behind it." Intriguingly, that makes Where Dolls Hang a rare game that is based on a true story,…
